title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page dated 13 June 1986, in the first draft ('première mouture') of the Analysis situs chapter, where Grothendieck is trying to axiomatize his 'tame topology' (the topologie modérée of the Esquisse d'un programme, §5).

(1) Bookkeeping. He lists which of his earlier axioms Cont.1, Cont.2, ... on 'contrées' are not yet expressed in the current formalism:
- Cont 3: finite dimension.
- Cont 4: 'admissibility', which he says is already visible from the axioms G.
- Cont 6: a disjointness criterion for 'lieux' (loci), deferred ('on y viendra').
- Cont 7: loci of distinct strata are disjoint, the usual partition axiom of a stratification.

(2) Change of viewpoint. He announces another restart, the 'quatrième mouture'. The primitive notion is now the set F of 'figures', carrying two partial orders:
- ≤, inclusion: F ≤ G (also written F ⊂ G) means F is a sub-figure of G.
- ≼, subdivision: F ≼ G means F subdivides (refines) G.
A contrée is the triple C = (F, ≤, ≼) subject to axioms still to be stated.

In modern terms this is a point-free, order-theoretic presentation of a tame or stratified space. Think of the figures as finite stratifications (or triangulations) of tame subsets. One order is 'is a closed/sub-stratified piece of'; the other is 'is a refinement of the same underlying locus'. The underlying 'lieu' of a figure would be recovered as an equivalence class under ≼, i.e. figures modulo common refinement.

The preceding page proves that, for the refinement order, the induced figure G' is the infimum of F' and G. That lemma motivates promoting refinement to a primitive order.

The next page begins the axioms for ≤:
- C1a: F is non-empty.
- C1b: every family bounded above (with respect to ≤) has a supremum, i.e. F is a bounded-complete poset.
- Consequently there is a least element, the empty figure.
- Families bounded above are called 'compatible' (co-figurées).
- Irreducible figures are the completely join-irreducible elements, which are to be identified with the multistrata.

The programme thus resembles a 'pointless topology' (in the spirit of frames and locales) adapted to stratified, tame geometry, with an extra refinement order playing the role of subdivision in PL topology.
errors: No mathematical error on this page: it consists of definitions and a to-do list. A latent gap is that ≼ is declared a partial order with no compatibility axioms yet linking it to ≤ (e.g. that subdivision preserves the underlying locus, or that sub-figures of a subdivision correspond to sub-figures of the subdivided figure). These are announced as 'axioms qu'on va examiner' and appear only on later pages.

Grothendieck writes 'deux relations d'ordre' but calls ≤ also 'l'inclusion'. Whether ≼ is antisymmetric (rather than a preorder) depends on figures being considered up to isomorphism; this is implicit and not checked here.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a 'contrée' (tame/stratified space) point-free, as a set of figures with two partial orders: inclusion (sub-figure) and subdivision (refinement)
ideas.modern_name: Bi-ordered poset presentation of stratified/tame spaces; cf. lattice of constructible sets in o-minimal structures, subcomplex vs. subdivision orders in PL topology, refinement of stratifications (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Lurie's exit paths)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984), realized via o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight 1980s). Point-free topology: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone. No standard bi-order axiomatization known to me.
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the tame topology goals; the 1986 'contrée' axiomatics appear to be unpublished (unsure whether partially discussed in secondary literature).

ideas.what: Making subdivision/refinement a primitive order relation alongside inclusion, motivated by the previous page's lemma that refinement admits infima ('G' est la Inf de F' et G')
ideas.modern_name: Refinement poset of stratifications / triangulations (common-refinement property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (common subdivision; Hauptvermutung context); refinement of stratifications in Whitney/Thom/Mather theory

ideas.what: Checklist of stratification axioms (finite dimension, admissibility, disjointness of loci, distinct strata disjoint) to be re-expressed in the new formalism
ideas.modern_name: Axioms of a (finite-dimensional) stratified space / tame stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather; o-minimal cell decomposition

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a purely order-theoretic foundation for tame topology: a 'contrée' is a set of figures with an inclusion order and a subdivision order satisfying axioms. On the next page these include bounded-completeness for inclusion, with multistrata as the irreducible figures. As far as I know, no one has developed such a two-order, point-free axiomatics of stratified/tame spaces. O-minimality took the route of definable sets in a first-order structure instead.
missed.quote: Prendre comme notion de base F, l'ens. des figures, avec les deux relations d'ordre ≤ (ou l'inclusion) et ≼ (la subdivision) ... Contrée (quatrième mouture!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A point-free, bi-ordered presentation could connect tame geometry with locale and topos theory. It could also connect with the combinatorial models of stratified spaces used in higher category theory (exit-path categories, refinement-invariance in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It would offer a framework where refinement invariance is built into the structure rather than imposed afterwards.

missed.claim: The inclusion order with sups of bounded families, and irreducible elements = multistrata, is a 'locale-like' structure. Adding a subdivision order recovers the underlying 'lieu' as a class modulo refinement. This implicitly links frame/locale theory to stratified/PL geometry, a connection the o-minimal literature did not make explicitly.
missed.quote: Si F ≼ G, on dit que F est une subdivision de G, ou que F subdivise G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This may suggest an algebraic/order-theoretic characterization of categories of stratified spaces up to refinement, relevant to constructible sheaves and exit-path ∞-categories.

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational, unpublished work on Grothendieck's tame-topology programme: a fourth restart replacing points/loci by a doubly ordered set of figures. The idea is original and apparently never developed in the literature. On this page, however, it is only definitions and intentions, with no results.
transcription_corrections: 'il reste par compte' should probably read 'il reste pour compte' (i.e. left over)
'Prendre comme une de base' should read 'Prendre comme notion de base'
'Cont 6 [-critère de-] disjonction ... des lieux': the image reads 'critère de disjonction des lieux', with 'critère de' added above the line rather than struck
'Cont 7 Deux lieux de strates [?] ... difficultés [?] sont disjoints' likely reads 'Deux lieux de strates (str.) différentes sont disjoints'
'je me décide encore une fois changer d'optique' is probably 'je me décide encore une fois à changer d'optique'
